raw_response:
I have farmed these 15 mu in Quzhou for 36 years. I never went to school, so I don't read papers or listen to strangers in clean clothes telling me what to do. I watch my neighbors. If Old Zhang's wheat looks greener than mine, I ask his wife what bags he bought, and I do the same. I have 10 mu that I plant wheat in the fall and then maize after the wheat comes off, and 5 mu of cotton. It is just me and my daughter-in-law at home now, so we cannot waste money on things that might not work.

For the wheat that is already in the ground, I put down one 100-jin bag of that 16-16-16 compound fertilizer per mu last fall, and now at green-up time I will spread another half bag of urea on top — that comes to about 35 jin of nitrogen per mu in total. I would rather put a little too much than see yellow leaves and regret it. A bad harvest means borrowing money; wasting some fertilizer just means eating less meat. I will run the well pump three times: now when it wakes up, again when the stems shoot up, and once more when the grain is filling. I spray for bugs twice. I don't touch the soil with a plough now — the wheat is already sleeping in its rows. I want 500 kilos per mu this year. Last year I got 480, so if the weather holds, 500 is possible.

After we cut the wheat in June, I hire the village rotary tiller for the 10 mu — costs 30 yuan per mu but saves my back. Then I plant hybrid maize seed, the kind in the yellow bag, about 3 jin per mu. Maize needs food to grow fast in summer. I give it the same as wheat: one bag of compound and half a bag of urea per mu, around 35 jin nitrogen, 16 jin phosphorus, 16 jin potassium per mu. I irrigate three times if it stays dry — tasseling time is the one you cannot miss. Two sprays for armyworm. I expect 600 kilos per mu. My nephew got 620 last year, so I want to match him.

The 5 mu of cotton is hard work, but the cotton money buys things we need. In April I plough it deep with the small tractor to break up the hard pan. I plant improved cotton seed, about 4 jin per mu — I mix last year's seed with new bags because cotton seed is expensive. I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu in the furrow, then side-dress with a smaller amount of urea when the flowers open. Total that is about 30 jin nitrogen, 16 jin phosphorus, 16 jin potassium per mu. I irrigate twice, in July and August when the bolls are swelling. I spray pesticide three times — cotton worms are greedy. I hope for 250 kilos of seed cotton per mu. Two years ago I got 260, last year only 240 because of the dry spell.

I don't try new tricks. Last year's plan worked, so this year's plan is the same. If the dealer tries to sell me fancy fertilizer, I walk away unless my neighbor used it first. That is how I stay safe.
